newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's 1996 capital account surplus $3.604 bln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's 1996 capital account surplus $3.604 bln.

text.p: Banco de Mexico on Monday said its capital account registered a $3.604 billion surplus in 1996, partly buoyed by direct foreign investment of $7.535 billion. It gave no comparative figures.

In a statement, the central bank said the loans and deposits item in the current account balance showed a net outflow of $11.729 billion, chiefly because of payments from the government to the U.S. Treasury, and from Banco de Mexico to the International Monetary Fund.

It said foreign portfolio investment was $14.154 billion, of which $2.995 billion was in the stock market, $907 million was in local currency debt, and $10.251 billion came from the issue of bonds abroad.
Foreign assets were $6.456 billion, much of which had been saved up for the pre-payment of loans to the U.S. Treasury and the IMF in January 1997.

The central bank said a combination of a $1.762 billion current account deficit, a $3.604 billion capital account surplus and a reduced negative $68 million balance in the errors and ommissions category meant international reserves grew $1.768 billion in 1996, including a slight adjustment for the revaluation of gold.
